subject: community-medicine
title: Chemical Vector Control: Malathion, Pyrethrum, Temephos, and Integrated Vector Management

steps.title: Malathion pharmacology and insecticidal action
steps.tx: Malathion is an organophosphorus insecticide widely deployed for adult mosquito control and outdoor thermal fogging. Absorbed through the insect cuticle, it undergoes metabolic activation to malaoxon, functioning through **malathion acetylcholinesterase inhibition mechanisms** that inactivate synaptic acetylcholinesterase; the resulting massive accumulation of acetylcholine across neural synapses causes continuous uncoordinated firing, tremors, convulsions, and respiratory paralysis, with mammalian safety conferred by rapid hydrolytic destruction by liver carboxylesterases.
steps.say: Malathion is an organophosphate insecticide that blocks acetylcholinesterase enzymes in insects. Excess acetylcholine overstimulates insect nerves, causing tremors and death while sparing human tissues.

nodes.label: Cuticular absorption and bioactivation to malaoxon
Accumulation of acetylcholine at neural synapses
Continuous firing, tremors, and insect paralysis

steps.tx: Malathion, an organophosphorus insecticide, is widely used against adult mosquitoes and in outdoor thermal fogging. It crosses the insect cuticle and is converted to malaoxon. Through **malathion acetylcholinesterase inhibition mechanisms**, synaptic acetylcholinesterase is inactivated, acetylcholine piles up, and nerves fire without pause. Tremors, convulsions, and respiratory paralysis follow. Mammals are relatively spared because liver carboxylesterases hydrolyse the compound quickly, which is why the same fog is far more lethal to the mosquito than to people nearby.
steps.say: Fogged malathion becomes malaoxon inside the mosquito and blocks acetylcholinesterase. Acetylcholine then drives continuous firing, tremor, and respiratory paralysis. Human liver enzymes break the poison down much faster.

steps.title: Natural pyrethrum and knock-down sprays
steps.tx: Extracted from the dried flower heads of Chrysanthemum cinerariaefolium, natural pyrethrum is an oleoresin containing six active insecticidal esters known as pyrethrins and cinerins. Functioning under **natural pyrethrum rapid knockdown kinetics**, the compound penetrates the insect nervous system within seconds to cause violent excitement and instant muscular collapse; because pyrethrins are rapidly detoxified by insect enzymes allowing eventual recovery, commercial formulations add piperonyl butoxide as an enzyme synergist.
steps.say: Pyrethrum is a natural extract from chrysanthemum flowers that causes instant insect knockdown. Adding piperonyl butoxide blocks detoxifying enzymes, ensuring mosquitoes do not recover.

left.title: Natural pyrethrum properties
points: Rapidly degraded by sunlight and heat

right.title: Synthetic pyrethroids
points: Used for indoor spraying and LLINs

steps.title: Temephos as a potable water larvicide
steps.tx: Controlling mosquito breeding inside domestic water storage reservoirs requires an insecticide of exceptionally low mammalian toxicity, satisfied by the **temephos potable larvicidal protocol**. Marketed as Abate, this organophosphorus compound acts selectively against mosquito larvae and aquatic crustaceans at an application concentration of one milligram per litre or one part per million, destroying larval populations within twenty-four hours without imparting odor, color, or toxic hazards to drinking water supplies.
steps.say: Temephos is an organophosphate larvicide safe for drinking water. Added at one part per million, it kills mosquito larvae in overhead tanks without harming humans or pets.

rows: WHO certified safe threshold for drinking water
Disrupts neuromuscular function in aquatic instars
Maintains active control despite domestic water withdrawal

steps.title: Mineral oils and mechanical surface films
steps.tx: Physical suppression of mosquito larvae in drains, septic tanks, and polluted stagnant pools relies on **larvicidal mineral oil surface films**, such as Malariol, diesel oil, and high-spreading monomolecular films. When sprayed over water surfaces at a rate of forty to ninety litres per hectare, the oil forms an unbroken monomolecular layer that reduces water surface tension, preventing larvae from anchoring and choking their spiracles to induce asphyxiation.
steps.say: Spraying mineral oils like Malariol over stagnant drains creates a thin surface film. This lowers surface tension and blocks mosquito breathing siphons, suffocating larvae quickly.

nodes.label: Oil sprayed over contaminated stagnant water
Rapid spread creates unbroken surface film
Blocks larval breathing siphons and spiracles
Larvae detach and drown from mechanical asphyxiation

steps.title: Bacterial larvicides and biocontrol
steps.tx: Environmental concerns surrounding synthetic chemicals spurred the development of bacterial biological larvicides comprising **Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis crystal endotoxins**, alongside Bacillus sphaericus. When ingested by feeding mosquito larvae, the delta-endotoxin protoxins are cleaved by alkaline midgut proteases into active pore-forming peptides; these insert into the larval midgut epithelial membranes, causing cellular swelling, lysis, and death within twenty-four hours while leaving fish, dragonflies, and humans entirely unharmed.
steps.say: Bacillus thuringiensis produces natural protein crystals that mosquito larvae eat. Alkaline gut fluids activate the crystals, destroying the insect stomach lining without harming fish or people.

left.title: Bacillus thuringiensis (BTI)
points: Highly effective against Aedes and Anopheles

right.title: Bacillus sphaericus
points: Highly potent against Culex larvae in drains

steps.title: Biological control with larvivorous fish
steps.tx: Biological predation of aquatic immature vectors utilizes **larvivorous fish biological predation**, primarily Gambusia affinis, the top minnow, and Poecilia reticulata, the guppy. A single adult Gambusia can voraciously consume up to three hundred mosquito larvae per day; Gambusia thrives in clean fresh water, garden fountains, and rural dug wells, whereas Poecilia exhibits remarkable resilience in organically polluted drainage channels and septic tanks.
steps.say: Gambusia and guppy fish eat hundreds of mosquito larvae daily. Gambusia thrives in clean wells, while hardy guppy fish clear mosquito larvae from dirty drains and septic tanks.

rows: 100 to 300 larvae consumed per fish per day
Thrives in foul water; continuous surface feeder

steps.tx: Aquatic mosquito larvae can be eaten rather than sprayed. **Larvivorous fish biological predation** uses mainly Gambusia affinis, the top minnow, and Poecilia reticulata, the guppy. One adult Gambusia may consume up to three hundred larvae in a day. Gambusia does best in clean fresh water, garden fountains, and rural dug wells. Poecilia survives in organically polluted drains and septic tanks, so the two species cover different breeding sites.
steps.say: Gambusia and guppies eat mosquito larvae, and one Gambusia can take hundreds in a day. Gambusia prefers clean wells and fountains, while guppies tolerate dirty drains and septic tanks.

steps.title: Space spraying versus indoor residual spraying
steps.tx: The strategic selection of adulticidal applications is dictated by epidemiological urgency under **adulticidal application strategy comparison**. During acute dengue or malaria epidemics, ultra-low-volume cold aerosol fogging or thermal fogging delivers space sprays of malathion or pyrethrum that contact and kill flying adults immediately to interrupt transmission; in endemic malaria zones, indoor residual spraying coats indoor wall surfaces with long-acting pyrethroids to kill resting vectors over months.
steps.say: Fogging is used during sudden outbreaks to kill flying adult mosquitoes immediately. Indoor wall spraying leaves a chemical layer that kills resting mosquitoes over many months.

left.title: Space spraying / fogging
points: Suspends in air to hit flying mosquitoes

right.title: Indoor residual spraying (IRS)
points: Coarse spray (100 to 200 microns) on walls
Kills resting mosquitoes for 3 to 6 months

steps.title: Long-lasting insecticidal nets and personal defense
steps.tx: Personal protection against nocturnal vectors incorporates **long-lasting insecticidal net deployment**, factory-treated with deltamethrin or alpha-cypermethrin bound into polyethylene fibres. LLINs provide physical exclusion combined with chemical barrier effects, surviving at least twenty standard washings and maintaining lethal contact toxicity for three years; topical application of diethyltoluamide repellent repels biting dipterans by interfering with olfactory antennal receptors.
steps.say: Long-lasting insecticidal nets protect against night bites for three years, withstanding repeated washing. Diethyltoluamide skin lotion confuses mosquito sensors, preventing bites outdoors.

steps.title: Integrated vector management framework
steps.tx: To overcome insecticide resistance and reduce environmental contamination, national health agencies adhere to the **integrated vector management framework**. This multi-faceted strategy combines environmental management through drainage and source reduction, rational chemical applications targeting larval and adult stages, biological predation with fish and bacteria, personal barrier defenses, and active community participation to achieve cost-effective and ecologically sustainable vector suppression.
steps.say: Integrated vector management combines drainage, selective spraying, predatory fish, and bed nets. Working together with communities provides sustainable vector control without excessive chemicals.
